sentences.text:
The facts leading to the filing of the instant petition are that on 15.03.2019 at about 3.00 p.m.,
when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EB 5945 near Honnenahalli gate situated on Chikkaballapura - Bengaluru road (NH7 bypass),
Chikkaballapura District, at that time a Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248 which was being driven by its driver in a rash & negligent manner came and dashed against the aforementioned motorcycle.
Due to the terrific impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries for which he has taken treatment as an inpatient and also undergone surgery.
The accidental injuries have caused permanent disability to him.
As the accident was caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248, the respondents are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Despite due service of notice of the petition upon him, the respondent No.1 failed to appear before this Tribunal.
As such he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EB5945 who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248 was not holding a valid &
effective driving licence at the time of the accident.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non compliance of section's 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
Rest of the petition averments are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a road traffic accident on 15.03.2019 at about 3.00 p.m., near Honnenahalli gate situated on Chikkaballapura - Bengaluru NH7 bypass road, Chikkaballapura District and sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
5.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 13 were marked on his behalf.
Dr.Nagaraj.
B.N s/o B.K.N.Swamy, Orthopedic Surgeon at SOADS, Bengaluru was examined as PW.2.
Ex's .P14 & 15 were marked through this witness.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.

sentences.text: Oral arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows : Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.1: The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sri.Munikrishnappa s/o Hanumantharayappa, the Chikkaballapura traffic police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248 for the offences punishable under sections 279, 337, 338 & 304(A) of IPC and 134 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
8. ISSUE NO.2 : The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhar card at Ex.P12 wherein his date of birth is reflected as 07.06.1982.
This indicates that he was aged 36 years as on the date of accident.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
In the absence of proof, taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner & his nature of work, if his income is assessed at Rs.10,000/ p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
9. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (i) Type III A open left distal femur comminuted fracture and (ii) Fracture of left proximal lateral tibia.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

The discharge summary issued by Victoria Hospital Hospital, Bengaluru (Ex.P10) indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 16.03.2019 to 30.03.2019 (15 days in total).

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : wound debridement & stabilization of fracture fragment with knee spanning Exfix & CRIF of lateral femoral condyle with 2 CC screws under SA on 17.03.2019.
10. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total physical disability of 61% to the left lower limb and 20% disability to the whole body.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the Sri. Mahesh. S.K vs Sri. Ram Singh Jangra on 20 April, 2023

3 physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 14%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 14%.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
11. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 15 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/ per day and a sum of Rs.18,000/ (1,200 X 15) is awarded under this head.
12. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.70,000/ under this head.
13. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 6 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.60,000/ (10,000 X 6) under this head.
14. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P11, the petitioner has spent Rs.9,633/
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,633/ which is rounded off to Rs.10,000/ towards medical expenses.
15. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '15'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.10,000/ p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,52,000/ (Rs.10,000 X 12 X 15 X 14/100) under this head.

16. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:

sentences.text: The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
What further deserves notice is that the femoral condyle fracture of the petitioner has resulted in malunion (as the said fracture was compound one).
A malunion is a fractured bone that has healed in an unacceptable position which causes significant impairment.
It can put increased stress on other joints causing pain.

Under such circumstances certainly there would be some sort of discomfort which would come in the way of effective discharge of the duties of the petitioner and for that he needs to be compensated suitably.
Hence a sum of Rs.80,000/ is awarded under this head.
17. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES :

The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo (i) removal of implants surgery and (ii) corrective surgery (with respect to malunion of the femoral condyle fracture) for which he may require Rs.60,000/.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgeries as suggested by the doctor, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.60,000/ towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

18. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 18,00000 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 70,00000 3 Loss of income during laid : 60,00000 up period 4
Medical expenses : 10,00000 5 Loss of future income due to : 2,52,00000 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 80,00000 happiness 7
Future medical and other : 60,00000 incidental expenses Total 5,50,00000 19.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
20. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Though the insurance company has contended that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the first respondent.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN05BL1248 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
21. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

sentences.text:
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,50,000/ (Rupees Five Lakhs Fifty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire award amount together with interest, shall be released to the petitioner by way of Epayment on proper identification and confirmation.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 20th day of April - 2023)
(Ashwini M.Hattiholi)
